lead_headline: Arvada Council Weighs Residency Rules for Sex Offenders, SVPs

type_specific.meeting_summary: Arvada City Council held a workshop to examine whether to draft an ordinance restricting where registered sex offenders and sexually violent predators may establish residence within city limits. Senior Assistant City Attorney Pedri Emory led the discussion, walking council through three core questions: who to restrict, which locations to restrict them from, and how far from those locations. No formal decisions were made, but most council members expressed support for a two-tiered approach with different buffer distances for sex offenders versus sexually violent predators.

workshop_topics.title: Sex Offender Residency Restrictions Ordinance
workshop_topics.tagline: Council weighs a two-tiered buffer zone ordinance covering 216 registered sex offenders and 3 sexually violent predators citywide
workshop_topics.lede: City Attorney Rachel Morris and Senior Assistant City Attorney Pedri Emory presented a framework for drafting an ordinance that would limit where registered sex offenders and sexually violent predators may establish a residence in Arvada. The discussion was prompted in part by a prior incident in which an offender moved immediately adjacent to a girls softball field near a city high school. Colorado currently has no statewide residency restriction law, and Arvada currently has no such ordinance. Staff noted that several neighboring cities — including Broomfield, Westminster, and Englewood — have enacted similar ordinances.

options.label: Apply restrictions to all registered sex offenders
options.summary: The ordinance would cover all 216 registered sex offenders in Arvada, applying a buffer distance from designated sensitive locations. All sexually violent predators are also sex offenders and would be included.
options.endorsement: Bob Fifer (as part of a tiered approach); Rebecka Lovisone (as part of a tiered approach)

options.label: Apply restrictions only to sexually violent predators (SVPs)
options.summary: The ordinance would cover only the three individuals currently adjudicated as sexually violent predators — a narrower group that has been judicially found highly likely to reoffend. Other sex offenders would not be subject to residency restrictions.

options.label: 500-foot buffer for sex offenders, 1,000-foot buffer for SVPs (tiered approach)
options.summary: A two-tiered ordinance would impose a 500-foot residency buffer for all registered sex offenders and a stricter 1,000-foot buffer for sexually violent predators. Restricted locations would include schools, parks, trails, childcare/daycare facilities, and open space, with some council members suggesting trails and parks apply only to the SVP tier.
options.endorsement: Bob Fifer, Rebecka Lovisone, Lauren Simpson (summary consensus)

options.label: Restrict by specific offense type (e.g., child-related vs. other offenses)
options.summary: Council asked whether the ordinance could target specific conviction types, such as offenses involving children, rather than all sex offenders. Staff advised against this approach due to legal complexity, preemption risk, and practical enforcement difficulties.
